D.11 Proof of Proposition 11

We prove Proposition 11 by verifying the following facts in turn:

  1. (a)

    If Assumption 5.1 holds for both ν1\nu_{1} and ν2\nu_{2}, then Assumption 5.1 holds for ν3:=ν1∪ν2\nu_{3}:=\nu_{1}\cup\nu_{2}.

  2. (b)

    Suppose that Assumption 5.2 holds for both ν1\nu_{1} and ν2\nu_{2}, and Assumption 5.1 holds for ν3=ν1∪ν2\nu_{3}=\nu_{1}\cup\nu_{2}. Then, Assumption 5.2 holds for ν3\nu_{3}.

  3. (c)

    If Assumption 5.2′ (or Assumption 5.3) holds for both ν1\nu_{1} and ν2\nu_{2}, then Assumption 5.2′ (or Assumption 5.3) holds for ν3=ν1∪ν2\nu_{3}=\nu_{1}\cup\nu_{2}.

  4. (d)

    If Assumption 5.4(a) holds for ν1\nu_{1} at an admissible value of γ\gamma, then it also holds for any ν2⊇ν1\nu_{2}\supseteq\nu_{1} at the same value of γ\gamma.

  5. (e)

    Suppose that Assumption 5.3 holds for ν1\nu_{1} and ν2\nu_{2} with ν2⊇ν1\nu_{2}\supseteq\nu_{1}. If Assumption 5.4(b) holds for ν1\nu_{1}, then Assumption 5.4(b) also holds for ν2\nu_{2} with γ†​(ν2)≥γ†​(ν1)\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{2})\geq\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{1}).

Combining these results, the first statement in Proposition 11 is obviously true. To prove the second statement, consider any two regular index sets ν1⊆ν2\nu_{1}\subseteq\nu_{2}. If Assumption 5.4(b) holds for ν1\nu_{1}, then Fact (e) implies that it also holds for ν2\nu_{2}. Consequently,

γ†​(ν1)=|ν1|≤|ν2|=γ†​(ν2).\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{1})=|\nu_{1}|\leq|\nu_{2}|=\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{2}).

Otherwise, Assumption 5.4(b) fails for ν1\nu_{1}, so the regularity of ν1\nu_{1} implies that Assumption 5.4(a) holds for ν1\nu_{1} at γ=γ†​(ν1)\gamma=\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{1}). By Fact (d), it also holds for ν2\nu_{2} at the same value of γ\gamma. Hence, γ†​(ν1)≤γ†​(ν2)\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{1})\leq\gamma_{\dagger}(\nu_{2}).

𝔼⁡[Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)∣X]=\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X\right]= 𝔼⁡[{π⁡(Z,X)−𝕊⁡[π]​(Z,X)}​Y∣X]𝔼⁡[A⁡{π⁡(Z,X)−𝕊⁡[π]​(Z,X)}∣X].\displaystyle\dfrac{\mathbb{E}\left[\left\{\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}[\pi](Z,X)\right\}Y\mid X\right]}{\mathbb{E}\left[A\left\{\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}[\pi](Z,X)\right\}\mid X\right]}.

This completes the proof of Theorem 1.

E.2 Proof of Theorem 2

For any function q⁡(Z,X)q(Z,X) that satisfies Equation (3.1), if ZZ is an 𝒮\mathcal{S}-PIV, then q⁡(Z,X)​A={q⁡(Z,X)−𝕊⁡[q]​(Z,X)}​Aq(Z,X)A=\{q(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}[q](Z,X)\}A is conditionally uncorrelated with Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)Y(1)-Y(0) given XX by the definition of 𝒮\mathcal{S}-PIV, and

𝔼⁡[q⁡(Z,X)​Y∣X]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[q(Z,X)Y\mid X\right]
=\displaystyle= 𝔼[q(Z,X)A{Y(1)−Y(0)}∣X]+𝔼[q(Z,X)𝔼[Y(0)∣Z,X]∣X]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[q(Z,X)A\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\mid X\right]+\mathbb{E}\left[q(Z,X)\mathbb{E}[Y(0)\mid Z,X]\mid X\right]
=\displaystyle= 𝔼⁡[q⁡(Z,X)​A∣X]×𝔼⁡[Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)∣X]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[q(Z,X)A\mid X\right]\times\mathbb{E}\left[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X\right] (By the definition of 𝒮\mathcal{S}-PIV)
=\displaystyle= 𝔼⁡[Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)∣X].\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X\right].

By integrating out XX, we complete the proof of Theorem 2.

E.3 Proof of Theorem 3

Proof of Theorem 3(a):

Suppose that q∈𝒮⟂q\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp} satisfies Equation (3.1). Then, for any qf​(Z,X):=f⁡(X)​q​(Z,X)q_{f}(Z,X):=f(X)q(Z,X) with f∈L∞​(X)f\in L_{\infty}(X), qf∈𝒮⟂q_{f}\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}, since for any s∈𝒮s\in\mathcal{S},

𝔼⁡[qf​(Z,X)​s​(Z,X)]=𝔼⁡[f⁡(X)​q​(Z,X)​s​(Z,X)]=𝔼⁡[f⁡(X)​𝔼​[q⁡(Z,X)​s​(Z,X)∣X]]=0.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[q_{f}(Z,X)s(Z,X)]=\mathbb{E}[f(X)q(Z,X)s(Z,X)]=\mathbb{E}[f(X)\mathbb{E}[q(Z,X)s(Z,X)\mid X]]=0.

Let g∈L2​(X)g\in L_{2}(X) be a function satisfying 𝔼⁡[A​d​(Z,X)​g​(X)]=0\mathbb{E}[Ad(Z,X)g(X)]=0 for all d∈𝒮⟂d\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}. Then, 𝔼⁡[A​qf​(Z,X)​g​(X)]=0\mathbb{E}[Aq_{f}(Z,X)g(X)]=0 for all f∈L∞​(X)f\in L_{\infty}(X) since qf∈𝒮⟂q_{f}\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}. Consequently,

0=𝔼⁡[A​qf​(Z,X)​g​(X)]=𝔼⁡[𝔼⁡[A​q​(Z,X)∣X]​f​(X)​g​(X)]=𝔼⁡[f⁡(X)​g​(X)], for all f∈L∞​(X).\displaystyle 0=\mathbb{E}[Aq_{f}(Z,X)g(X)]=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[Aq(Z,X)\mid X]f(X)g(X)]=\mathbb{E}[f(X)g(X)],\text{ for all $f\in L_{\infty}(X)$.}

Then g⁡(X)≡0g(X)\equiv 0, because L∞​(X)L_{\infty}(X) is dense in L2​(X)L_{2}(X). This indicates that the 𝒮\mathcal{S}-completeness condition holds. ∎

Proof of Theorem 3(b):

If there exist two distinct solutions h1o​(X)h_{1}^{o}(X) and h2o​(X)h_{2}^{o}(X) to Equation (3.2), then

𝔼⁡[d⁡(Z,X)​{Y−A​h1o​(X)}]=𝔼⁡[d⁡(Z,X)​{Y−A​h2o​(X)}]=0,∀d∈𝒮⟂.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\big[d(Z,X)\{Y-Ah_{1}^{o}(X)\}\big]=\mathbb{E}\big[d(Z,X)\{Y-Ah_{2}^{o}(X)\}\big]=0,\qquad\forall\,d\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}.
⟹\displaystyle\Longrightarrow\quad 𝔼⁡[A​d​(Z,X)​{h1o​(X)−h2o​(X)}]=0,∀d∈𝒮⟂.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\big[Ad(Z,X)\{h_{1}^{o}(X)-h_{2}^{o}(X)\}\big]=0,\qquad\forall\,d\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}.

From the 𝒮\mathcal{S}-completeness condition, we know that h1o​(X)≡h2o​(X)h_{1}^{o}(X)\equiv h_{2}^{o}(X). Therefore, the solution to Equation (3.2) is unique. ∎

Proof of Theorem 3(c):

We directly show that

𝔼⁡[{π⁡(Z,X)−𝕊⁡[π]​(Z,X)}​{Y−A​𝔼​[Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)∣X]}]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\{\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}[\pi](Z,X)\}\{Y-A\mathbb{E}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X]\}]

=\displaystyle= 𝔼⁡[A⁡{π⁡(Z,X)−𝕊⁡[π]​(Z,X)}​{Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)−𝔼⁡[Y⁡(1)−Y⁡(0)∣X]}]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[A\{\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}[\pi](Z,X)\}\{Y(1)-Y(0)-\mathbb{E}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X]\}]

The final equality follows from 𝔼{Y(0)∣Z,X}∈𝒮\mathbb{E}\{Y(0)\mid Z,X\}\in\mathcal{S}, as stated in Definition 2.4(a), the fact that π⁡(Z,X)−𝕊⁡[π]​(Z,X)∈𝒮⟂\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}[\pi](Z,X)\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}, and Definition 2.4(b), which implies that

E.4 Proof of Theorem 4

We parametrize the marginal density pO​(o)p_{O}(o) by a differentiable parametric path {pO(θ)​(o):θ∈[−c,c]}\{p_{O}^{(\theta)}(o):\theta\in[-c,c]\}, for some sufficiently small constant c>0c>0, such that pO(0)​(o)=pO​(o)p_{O}^{(0)}(o)=p_{O}(o). This construction defines a regular parametric submodel along which pathwise derivatives are taken. We define the score function sθ(o):=∇θlog{pO(θ)(o)}|θ=0s_{\theta}(o):=\nabla_{\theta}\log\{p_{O}^{(\theta)}(o)\}\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}, and denote expectations under pO(θ)p_{O}^{(\theta)} by 𝔼θ​[f⁡(O)]:=∫f⁡(o)​pO(θ)​(o)​𝑑o\mathbb{E}^{\theta}[f(O)]:=\int f(o)p_{O}^{(\theta)}(o)\mathrm{d}o. We further let 𝕊(θ):L2​(O)→𝒮\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}:L_{2}(O)\to\mathcal{S} denote a projection operator defined under the model pO(θ)p_{O}^{(\theta)}:

𝕊(θ)​[f]:=arg⁡mins∈𝒮​𝔼(θ)​[{f⁡(O)−s⁡(Z,X)}2],\displaystyle\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f]:=\underset{s\in\mathcal{S}}{\arg\min}\mathbb{E}^{(\theta)}[\left\{f(O)-s(Z,X)\right\}^{2}],

which will be used to characterize pathwise derivatives along this parametric submodel.

Next, we introduce a useful lemma for conducting semiparametric analysis.

=\displaystyle= 𝔼[{π(Z,X)−𝕊γ[π](Z,X)}A|Z[−ν0],X]×𝔼[AY(0)∣U,Z[−ν0],X]𝔼[A∣Z[−ν0],X].\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\{\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}_{\gamma}[\pi](Z,X)\}A\middle|Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X\right]\times\dfrac{\mathbb{E}[AY(0)\mid U,Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X]}{\mathbb{E}[A\mid Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X]}. (By Assumption 5.2)

=\displaystyle= 𝔼[{π(Z,X)−𝕊γ[π](Z,X)}A|Z[−ν0],X]×𝔼[Y(0)∣A=1,Z[−ν0],X]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\{\pi(Z,X)-\mathbb{S}_{\gamma}[\pi](Z,X)\}A\middle|Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X\right]\times\mathbb{E}[Y(0)\mid A=1,Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X]

−𝔼k​[{Π⁡(Z,X)−ρ𝒮,Πo​(Z,X)}​{A−δ𝒮o​(Z,X)}]\displaystyle-\mathbb{E}_{k}\left[\left\{\Pi(Z,X)-\rho_{\mathcal{S},\Pi}^{o}(Z,X)\right\}\left\{A-\delta_{\mathcal{S}}^{o}(Z,X)\right\}\right]

+𝔼k​[{Π⁡(Z,X)−ρ^𝒮,Π(n,−k)​(Z,X)}​{A−δ^𝒮(n,−k)​(Z,X)}]\displaystyle+\mathbb{E}_{k}\left[\left\{\Pi(Z,X)-\hat{\rho}_{\mathcal{S},\Pi}^{(n,-k)}(Z,X)\right\}\left\{A-\hat{\delta}_{\mathcal{S}}^{(n,-k)}(Z,X)\right\}\right]
−𝔼k​[{Π⁡(Z,X)−ρ𝒮,Πo​(Z,X)}​{A−δ𝒮o​(Z,X)}]\displaystyle-\mathbb{E}_{k}\left[\left\{\Pi(Z,X)-\rho_{\mathcal{S},\Pi}^{o}(Z,X)\right\}\left\{A-\delta_{\mathcal{S}}^{o}(Z,X)\right\}\right]

Appendix F Proof of Lemmas

F.1 Proof of Lemma 5.1

Proof of Lemma 5.1(a):

Under Assumptions 5.1 and 5.2, we have:

𝔼[Y(0)∣Z,X]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[Y(0)\mid Z,X] =𝔼[𝔼[Y(0)∣U,Z,X]∣Z,X]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[Y(0)\mid U,Z,X]\mid Z,X]
=𝔼[𝔼[Y(0)∣U,Z[−ν0],X]∣Z,X]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[Y(0)\mid U,Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X]\mid Z,X] (by Assumption 5.2)
=𝔼[𝔼[Y(0)∣U,Z[−ν0],X]∣Z[−ν0],X]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[Y(0)\mid U,Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X]\mid Z_{[-\nu_{0}]},X] (by Assumption 5.1)

F.2 Proof of Lemma D.1

We define D_γ := { d∈L_2(Z,X): E[d(Z,X)∣Z_[-ν],X]=0,  for all —ν—≥γ}. We directly verify that L2​(Z,X)L_{2}(Z,X) admits an orthogonal decomposition into 𝒮γ\mathcal{S}_{\gamma} and 𝒟γ\mathcal{D}_{\gamma}.

For any ν⊆⟨dZ⟩\nu\subseteq\langle d_{Z}\rangle, define the map ℱ[ν]:L2​(Z,X)→L2​(Z,X)\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}:L_{2}(Z,X)\to L_{2}(Z,X) by ℱ[ν][d](Z,X)=𝔼[d(Z,X)∣Z[−ν],X].\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}[d](Z,X)=\mathbb{E}\left[d(Z,X)\mid Z_{[-\nu]},X\right]. Define the kernel and range of ℱ[ν]\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]} as

Ker⁡{ℱ[ν]}\displaystyle\operatorname{Ker}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\} :={d∈L2​(Z,X):ℱ[ν]​[d]=0},\displaystyle:=\left\{d\in L_{2}(Z,X):\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}[d]=0\right\},
Range⁡{ℱ[ν]}\displaystyle\operatorname{Range}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\} :={ℱ[ν]​[d]:d∈L2​(Z,X)}=L2​(Z[−ν],X).\displaystyle:=\left\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}[d]:d\in L_{2}(Z,X)\right\}=L_{2}(Z_{[-\nu]},X).

Because ℱ[ν]\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]} is the orthogonal projection onto L2​(Z[−ν],X)L_{2}(Z_{[-\nu]},X), its range is closed and Ker⁡{ℱ[ν]}⟂=Range⁡{ℱ[ν]}.\operatorname{Ker}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\}^{\perp}=\operatorname{Range}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\}. Since 𝒟γ=⋂ν:|ν|≥γKer{ℱ[ν]},\mathcal{D}_{\gamma}=\bigcap_{\nu:|\nu|\geq\gamma}\operatorname{Ker}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\}, we obtain

𝒟γ⟂\displaystyle\mathcal{D}_{\gamma}^{\perp} ={⋂ν:|ν|≥γKer{ℱ[ν]}}⟂=∑ν:|ν|≥γKer{ℱ[ν]}⟂¯\displaystyle=\left\{\bigcap_{\nu:|\nu|\geq\gamma}\operatorname{Ker}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\}\right\}^{\perp}=\overline{\sum_{\nu:|\nu|\geq\gamma}\operatorname{Ker}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\}^{\perp}}
=∑ν:|ν|≥γRange{ℱ[ν]}¯=∑ν:|ν|≥γL2(Z[−ν],X)¯=𝒮γ.\displaystyle=\overline{\sum_{\nu:|\nu|\geq\gamma}\operatorname{Range}\{\mathcal{F}_{[\nu]}\}}=\overline{\sum_{\nu:|\nu|\geq\gamma}L_{2}(Z_{[-\nu]},X)}=\mathcal{S}_{\gamma}.

Because 𝒟γ\mathcal{D}_{\gamma} is an intersection of closed subspaces, it is closed. Taking orthogonal complements therefore gives 𝒮γ⟂=𝒟γ.\mathcal{S}_{\gamma}^{\perp}=\mathcal{D}_{\gamma}. Hence, L2​(Z,X)=𝒮γ⊕𝒟γ,L_{2}(Z,X)=\mathcal{S}_{\gamma}\oplus\mathcal{D}_{\gamma}, which completes the proof of Lemma D.1.

F.3 Proof of Lemma E.1

We define ⟨f,g⟩θ:=𝔼(θ)​[f⁡(O)​g​(O)]\langle f,g\rangle_{\theta}:=\mathbb{E}^{(\theta)}[f(O)g(O)], which is an inner product in L2(θ)​(O):={f:𝔼(θ)​[f​(O)2]<∞}L_{2}^{(\theta)}(O):=\{f:\mathbb{E}^{(\theta)}[f(O)^{2}]<\infty\}. We start from the definition of a projection operator. That is, for all g∈𝒮g\in\mathcal{S},

𝔼(θ)​[{f⁡(O)−𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)}​g​(Z,X)]=⟨f−𝕊(θ)​[f],g⟩θ≡0.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}^{(\theta)}[\{f(O)-\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\}g(Z,X)]=\langle f-\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f],\;g\rangle_{\theta}\equiv 0.

We then take the derivative with respect to θ\theta and derive that

0=\displaystyle 0= ∇θ𝔼(θ)​[{f⁡(O)−𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)}​g​(Z,X)]​|θ=0\displaystyle\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{E}^{(\theta)}[\{f(O)-\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\}g(Z,X)]\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}
=\displaystyle= 𝔼⁡[{f⁡(O)−𝕊⁡[f]​(Z,X)}​g​(Z,X)​sθ​(O)]+𝔼⁡[−∇θ𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)​|θ=0​g​(Z,X)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\{f(O)-\mathbb{S}[f](Z,X)\}g(Z,X)s_{\theta}(O)]+\mathbb{E}[-\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}g(Z,X)]
=\displaystyle= 𝔼⁡[𝕊⁡[{f−𝕊⁡[f]}​sθ]​(Z,X)​g​(Z,X)]+𝔼⁡[−∇θ𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)​|θ=0​g​(Z,X)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{S}[\{f-\mathbb{S}[f]\}s_{\theta}](Z,X)g(Z,X)]+\mathbb{E}[-\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}g(Z,X)]
=\displaystyle= 𝔼⁡[{𝕊⁡[{f−𝕊⁡[f]}​sθ]​(Z,X)−∇θ𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)​|θ=0}​g​(Z,X)].\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\left\{\mathbb{S}[\{f-\mathbb{S}[f]\}s_{\theta}](Z,X)-\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}\right\}g(Z,X)\right]. (F.1)

The third step follows since g∈𝒮g\in\mathcal{S} and 𝔼⁡[f⁡(O)​g​(Z,X)]=𝔼⁡[𝕊⁡[f]​(Z,X)​g​(Z,X)]\mathbb{E}[f(O)g(Z,X)]=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{S}[f](Z,X)g(Z,X)] by the property of projection operator. Now since Equation (F.1) holds for all g∈𝒮g\in\mathcal{S}, it follows that

𝕊⁡[{f−𝕊⁡[f]}​sθ]​(Z,X)−∇θ𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)​|θ=0∈𝒮⟂.\displaystyle\mathbb{S}[\{f-\mathbb{S}[f]\}s_{\theta}](Z,X)-\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}.

Simultaneously, 𝕊⁡[{f−𝕊⁡[f]}​sθ]​(Z,X)−∇θ𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)​|θ=0∈𝒮\mathbb{S}[\{f-\mathbb{S}[f]\}s_{\theta}](Z,X)-\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}\in\mathcal{S} by definition of 𝕊\mathbb{S} and the assumption that the derivative belongs to 𝒮\mathcal{S}. Therefore,

𝕊⁡[{f−𝕊⁡[f]}​sθ]​(Z,X)−∇θ𝕊(θ)​[f]​(Z,X)​|θ=0∈𝒮⟂​⋂𝒮={0}.\displaystyle\mathbb{S}[\{f-\mathbb{S}[f]\}s_{\theta}](Z,X)-\nabla_{\theta}\mathbb{S}^{(\theta)}[f](Z,X)\evaluated{}_{\theta=0}\in\mathcal{S}^{\perp}\bigcap\mathcal{S}=\{0\}.

This completes the proof of Lemma E.1.
